app_note: Enriched wheat flour is refined wheat flour with selected nutrients added back.
Whole wheat flour includes bran germ and endosperm from the wheat kernel.
Semolina is a coarse durum wheat product prized for pasta texture.
Rye flour gives dense earthy breads and supports sourdough-style baking.
risk_note: Contains gluten-related proteins and is not gluten-free.

app_note: Barley flour and malted barley add grain flavor and can affect browning.
risk_note: Contains gluten-related proteins and is not gluten-free.

app_note: Oat flour adds mild sweetness and moisture to baked foods.
risk_note: Oats may need certified gluten-free status due to cross-contact.

app_note: Rice flour is common in gluten-free baking and Asian noodles.
risk_note: Texture can be gritty if not finely milled.

app_note: Corn flour is finely ground corn and differs from cornstarch.
risk_note: Usually gluten-free but cross-contact is possible.

app_note: Masa harina is a traditional corn flour used for tortillas and tamales.
risk_note: Distinct from ordinary corn flour because of its culinary role.

app_note: Tapioca flour and tapioca starch are often the same ingredient on labels.
risk_note: Adds chew and stretch in gluten-free foods.

app_note: Potato starch thickens quickly and can help coatings become crisp.
risk_note: Different from potato flour which includes more whole-potato solids.

app_note: Arrowroot starch is used for clear glossy thickening in some sauces and desserts.
risk_note: Often chosen for simple-label starch needs.

app_note: Cassava flour is made from cassava root and includes more whole-root material than tapioca starch.
Sorghum flour is a gluten-free grain flour with mild earthy flavor.
risk_note: Often blended with starches for better baking texture.

app_note: Millet flour comes from small-seeded grains used in many traditional diets.
risk_note: Can add a slightly sweet or nutty note.

app_note: Buckwheat is not wheat and is naturally gluten-free when uncontaminated.
Quinoa flour adds protein and earthy flavor to gluten-free foods.
risk_note: Can taste bitter if not prepared well by the supplier.

app_note: Almond flour adds fat protein and tenderness to baked goods.
Coconut flour absorbs a lot of water and behaves differently from grain flour.
risk_note: Coconut allergen classification varies by jurisdiction.
